== Biography ==
William was born about 1804.
<ref>Based on death 1898 age 94 -- although death ages of this time can be very unreliable.</ref>

His wife was called Mary Henry.
<ref>See attached death certificate of their son James - citing parents William Glasgow / Mary Glasgow nee Henry.</ref>

He passed away 9 April 1898 at Montober.  
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/10cb264267060 William Glasgow, 1898, Cookstown, 94] at Irish Civil Registration - Deaths</ref>
<ref>PRONI Will Calendars: Probate of the Will of William Glasgow late of Montober County Tyrone Farmer who died 9 April 1898 granted at Armagh to Allen Glasgow of Drumnamalta and Robert J. Charles of Beltoninanean both said County Farmers.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2915]] is assessed at 31% (possible). William’s c 1804 generation fits the inherited William-2915 father and the broader proposed Cookstown family. The held account establishes William with wife Mary Henry, but their son’s record names those parents only and gives no grandfather. No specific holding or named-relative record joins the two Williams.

Possible 31%; existing pedigree retained, while the older William’s local identity remains unproved.

Next useful test: Find William and Mary Henry’s marriage or a sibling connection.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-585 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-585]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


In his will he mentions daughter Jane living with him, and the will was witnessed by [[Glasgow-692|David Glasgow]] of Beltonanean, and John Henry of Drumnamalta..  On his death record the witness is "David Glasgow, Montober" which is supposed to be the witness's his place of residence. So either he put the wrong place (I have seen that before) or possibly not the right parents?

He appears in the 1860 Griffith's Valuation for Tyrone, as William Glasgow at  Montober. He wasn't in the 1827 tithe applotment book; that had only David and John at Montober.

There was a different William Glasgow who also married a Mary Henry in 1846, see [[Glasgow-1737|William Glasgow (abt.1824-)]].  I do not believe these two people are the same because:
* That William gave his age as 22 , Bachelor on the 1846 marriage record.
* This William has children starting from 1827.

The death of William Glasgow was registered on 9 April 1898 in Cookstown, aged 94.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI civil death index], William Glasgow, 9 April 1898, aged 94, Cookstown registration district, D/1898/99/1009/16/261.</ref>

A possible identification concerns William Glasgow, uncle in the Cookstown mill case. Benjamin’s evidence says “witness’s uncle, Mr. Glasgow, sen.”. William is the separate case-context identification of the senior man, distinct from co-plaintiff William; extending the uncle relationship to that co-plaintiff depends on the qualified brother inference.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 22 July 1858, p.3; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574459/ record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns William Glasgow, uncle in the Cookstown mill case. William Glasgow of Cookstown retired from business and received a silver ewer and cake basket at the Imperial Hotel, Belfast, on 1 January 1856. This merchant could be the later uncle; the retirement report does not state the nephews or an age.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 4 January 1856, p.1; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390544967/ record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns William Glasgow, uncle in the Cookstown mill case. The named witness Benjamin Glasgow identifies the late Robert Glasgow as his father, says he managed his father’s mill from 1850, and dates Robert’s death to 1856. Benjamin’s evidence describes a companion as “witness’s uncle, Mr. Glasgow, sen.”; identification as William belongs to the separate case context, not this quotation.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 22 July 1858, p.3, Benjamin’s sworn testimony; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574459/ record].</ref> Certain documentary father–son relationship; identification of Robert with [[Glasgow-2656]] or [[Glasgow-3941]] remains qualified. Counsel’s reference to Robert’s sons supports a qualified brother inference for co-plaintiff William. The uncle’s paternal or maternal side and all mothers are unstated. No parents are established for [[Glasgow-2058|John Glasgow]]. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns William Glasgow, uncle in the Cookstown mill case. Wm. Glasgow appears among Cookstown collectors and again among Cookstown donors in the 10-shillings-each list for the new Claggan Presbyterian Church, opened on 15 October 1846.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 10 November 1846, p.4, Claggan Presbyterian Church opening; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390561508/ record].</ref> Cookstown is supplied by the shared group punctuation; the separate Inishrush entry concerns James M’Caw. No age, trade or kin is stated. The occurrence is unassigned among the same-name Cookstown accounts and does not identify the later uncle or younger mill partner. The identification remains uncertain.
